Relevant part of the order of the order reads as under :-
"Quashing of offence or criminal proceedings on the ground of settlement between an offender and victim is not the same thing as compounding of offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Sadik Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: They are different and not interchangeable.
sentences._hearing_file: Sadik Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Strictly speaking, the power of compounding of offences given to a court under Section 320 is materially different from the quashing of criminal proceedings by the High Court in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction.
sentences._hearing_file: Sadik Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: In compounding of offences, power of a criminal court is circumscribed by the provisions contained in Section 320 and the court is guided solely and squarely thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of opinion by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence or criminal proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by the material on record as to whether the ends of justice would justify such exercise of power although the ultimate consequence may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.
sentences._hearing_file: Sadik Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: B.S.Joshi, Nikhil Merchant, Manoj Sharma and Shiji do illustrate the principle that the High Court may quash criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent power under Section 482 of the Code and Section 320 does not limit or affect the powers of the High Court under Section 482.
sentences._hearing_file: Sadik Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Can it be said that by quashing criminal proceedings in B.S.Joshi, Nikhil Merchant, Manoj Sharma and Shiji this Court has compounded the non- compoundable offences indirectly?

opennyai_summary.13_September_2024__facts:
Thereafter, on 07.01.2024 and 10.01.2024 he not only raped her,
but also made a video and, thereafter, threatened to make it viral and to kill the complainant.
On this intimation, crime was registered on the very same date at police station Bahodapur, District Gwalior bearing Crime No.469/2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 377, 323, 294, 506, 34 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The allegation against the applicant is of 376 and 377 of IPC and the offence under said section is not made out against the present applicant as the present applicant and prosecutrix are husband and wife.
The FIR is delayed by approximately six months and no satisfactory explanation has been given by the prosecutrix/complainant.
Such inordinate delay in lodging the FIR points towards the fact that it was registered after post deliberations, consultation and discussions of prosecutrix with her family members and after taking legal advice, as would be evident from the F.I.R. that at the time of submitting complaint, the complainant was accompanied with her counsel just to harass the present applicant.
The FIR got registered after the divorce notices were sent to the prosecutrix/complainant by her husband/co-accused Sadik on 27.04.2024, 29.05.2024 and 01.07.2024 respectively.
Under these circumstances, the applicant prays for anticipatory bail.
Further, as per the allegations family members of applicant had taken obscene photos of complainant and had threatened her of defaming.
Since investigation is still going on, the applicant doesn't deserves to be granted anticipatory bail.
opennyai_summary.13_September_2024__ANALYSIS:
After hearing counsels for the parties and taking over all facts and circumstances of FIR, 161 and 164 Statements, this Court finds strength in the arguments advance by the counsels for the respondents and observes that the case of the present applicant being husband is different from that of the co-accused who had been granted bail.
Thus, in view of the above observations, no case of grant of anticipatory bail is made out in favor of the present applicant.
opennyai_summary.13_September_2024__decision: 13. Accordingly, the present application is hereby dismissed.

It could thus be seen that the learned three- Judge Bench of this Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303 held that B.S. Joshi v. State of Haryana,

The Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:31780 3 MCRC-44351-2025 Anr. reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303 after considering the provisions of Section 320 and 482 of the Cr.P.C held that the compounding can he permitted in a non- compoundable offence.
In compounding of offences, power of a criminal court is circumscribed by the provisions contained in Section 320 and the court is guided solely and squarely thereby while, on the other hand, the formation of opinion by the High Court for quashing a criminal offence or criminal proceeding or criminal complaint is guided by the material on record as to whether the ends of justice would justify such exercise of power although the ultimate consequence may be acquittal or dismissal of indictment.
Where the victim and offender have compromised disputes essentially civil and personal in nature, the High Court can exercise its power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. to quash the criminal proceedings.
8. In the case of State of M.P. Vs. Laxmi Narayan (2019) 5 SCC 688, a Three Judge Bench of the Apex Court discussed the earlier judgments of the Apex Court and laid down the principles in para-15.
In the case of Jaswant Singh vs. State of Punjab and Anr., Criminal Appeal No.1233 of 2021 (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.7072 of 2021 decided on 20.10.2021), the Apex Court held in para 61 that criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominatingly civil flavour stand on a different footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising from commercial, financial,
mercantile, civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc.
, the proceedings can be quashed in exercise of the powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compounding.
